NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Experienced healers want to always explain treatments and ask before acting: make it the rule, or trust each healer's judgment.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject), the eldest midwife, has called the healers together. Too often, (subject.he/she) says, the healers simply do things to people without telling them why. (friend) says sometimes there is no time to explain. What should the healers decide?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The healers agree: explain, ask, and only skip it when someone's life depends on it. The patients are surprised to be asked. Some of them say no, which takes getting used to. Most say yes, and seem less frightened.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The healers leave it to each one's judgment. (subject) explains everything, slowly. (friend) explains when there is time. The patients learn which healer to ask for.
